title: The Halo of Galaxy Messier 87
caption: The halo of the giant elliptical galaxy Messier 87, imaged by the Burrell Schmidt Telescope
celestial: Messier 87 · constellation Virgo · about 50 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: Chris Mihos (Case Western Reserve University)/ESO[See also: http://www.eso.org/public/images/eso0919a/]

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A huge, faint halo of light surrounds the giant elliptical galaxy Messier 87 in this very deep image, with many other galaxies scattered around it. These neighbors belong to the Virgo Cluster, and Messier 87 is the biggest of them all.

Elliptical galaxies are smooth, rounded collections of mostly older stars, and they are thought to grow partly by swallowing smaller galaxies. The halo holds evidence of just that. In the upper right part of the halo there is an excess of light, and it lines up with a clue from inside the galaxy, the way its planetary nebulae are moving.

Together, these are the final surviving traces of a medium-sized galaxy that collided with Messier 87 not long ago, in cosmic terms. Apart from this faint excess of light and the telltale motions of the planetary nebulae, little else records that the smaller galaxy was ever there.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (96.66 x 96.63 arcminutes) and distance (50 million light years), the frame spans roughly 1.4 million × 1.4 million light-years. Its light set out about 50 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This deep image was made with the Burrell Schmidt Telescope in visible light. The source does not publish the color mapping.
understand.eye: The halo is far too faint to see by eye, and only a very deep image that gathers light for a long time reveals it.

explore: At the top right of the frame sit two galaxies that astronomers have nicknamed "the Eyes". Like the many other galaxies scattered around Messier 87 here, they are members of the Virgo Cluster.
alt: A giant elliptical galaxy with a faint extended halo, surrounded by many other galaxies, including two at top right.
